chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abu Talib, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performs Hajj by incurring debt, and he had performed the Hajj of Islam. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, Allah will pay off the debt for him, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.سَيَقْضِي عَنْهُ: He will pay off/settle for him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Hajj if one has taken a debt to fund it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that incurring debt to perform the obligatory Hajj is permissible, with the promise that Allah will settle the debt for the pilgrim. This ruling highlights the high spiritual value of Hajj in Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing the fulfillment of the divine pillar even if it requires temporary financial burden, reflecting the concept of divine facilitation (*taysir*) for those who strive in worship.
